source: AI-assisted content generation (ChatGPT), synthesized from MAFF CAMAgriMarket/Cam Agri Hub documentation, FAO Cambodia
text: Market information helps a Preah Vihear smallholder compare buyers before accepting an offer — the useful question is not "what is today's highest price" but "what net price can I realistically receive after transport, grading, packaging, losses, commissions, and other costs." A farmer who knows only one buyer's price cannot judge whether it's competitive; comparing at least two offers and calculating net return after transport and deductions is more useful than comparing quoted prices alone. Farmers should distinguish farm-gate price from market/wholesale price (someone already paid the transport, loading, sorting, and market fees embedded in the higher number), and should not treat a reported market price for one quality/variety as applying automatically to their own mixed or lower-grade product. Cambodia's Ministry of Agriculture operates CAMAgriMarket, a mobile tool for agricultural traders and market-price monitoring, and MAFF's newer Cam Agri Hub aggregates several digital agricultural tools — these can be useful but a displayed price should still be verified against the farmer's actual product, location, quality, and date. During the wet season (roughly May–October), muddy roads and difficult transport can make a buyer's farm-gate collection more valuable than a slightly higher price requiring the farmer to transport the product; during the dry season (roughly November–April), transport may be easier but water and heat constraints affect production and livestock. A simple notebook recording date, product, buyer, quoted price, deductions, transport cost, and final amount received is more useful than relying on memory or a single reported number. No specific current Preah Vihear price should be invented — verified local sources should be used or the farmer asked directly.
